introduction-navigating-the-paradox-of-c.core: The CNCF landscape offers hundreds of tools for every platform layer, and too much choice paralyses teams and leads to fragile, bespoke stacks. CNOE (Cloud Native Operational Excellence) provides an opinionated, community-validated blueprint for building IDPs.

first_principles.problem: A platform team spends six months evaluating tools and still argues about which GitOps engine, portal and IaC tool to combine.
truths: Many companies solve the same integration problems.
derivation: Use a **reference architecture** instead of starting blank.

analogy.title: A restaurant menu with a chef's tasting option
analogy.story: Instead of choosing from 300 dishes, you start with a curated menu that's known to work together.
analogy.breaks: A reference architecture isn't a perfect fit for everyone, so adapt it.

example.title: Decision time saved
flow: With CNOE: start with Backstage + ArgoCD + Crossplane

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Focus moves to integration and value.

check.a: The paradox of choice and fragmentation in assembling an IDP from the vast CNCF landscape.

the-cnoe-philosophy-opinionated-but-open.core: CNOE is opinionated (it recommends specific tools and integration patterns proven by large adopters like AWS, Adobe and Autodesk) but open, with modular capabilities so organisations can swap components without abandoning the architecture.

first_principles.problem: Every company builds a bespoke IDP with no shared patterns, duplicating integration effort and creating fragile stacks.
derivation: Define **capabilities** (portal, GitOps, IaC, secrets, policy, observability).

analogy.title: A modular kitchen design
analogy.story: A recommended layout with standard fittings, where you can still choose your own oven brand.
analogy.breaks: Too much swapping erodes the benefit of a shared blueprint.

example.title: Swapping a component
example.outcome: a shared blueprint adapted to local needs.

check.q: What does 'opinionated but open' mean in CNOE?
check.a: It recommends specific proven tools and patterns while allowing components to be swapped within each capability.

the-core-cnoe-stack.core: CNOE's reference stack typically combines Backstage (portal), Argo CD (GitOps delivery), Argo Workflows (pipelines), Crossplane and/or Terraform (infrastructure provisioning), Keycloak (identity), External Secrets (secrets) and Kyverno or OPA (policy), all integrated on Kubernetes.

first_principles.problem: Teams know the tools individually but not how to combine them into a coherent platform.
truths: Kubernetes provides a common control plane.

analogy.title: A band's line-up
analogy.story: Each instrument plays its part, and together they make the song.
analogy.breaks: Running the full stack needs skills and operational investment.

example.title: A template-to-running-app flow
flow: Argo CD syncs app to cluster
example.outcome: you know how the pieces fit.

check.q: Which CNOE component typically handles GitOps delivery?

why-operational-excellence.core: CNOE is named for operational excellence, not tools: the goal is outcomes like reliable delivery, security, developer productivity and reduced toil. Tools are means to those ends, and the reference architecture is judged by the outcomes it enables.

first_principles.problem: Platform teams chase tools ('we need Backstage') rather than outcomes ('we need onboarding under a day').
truths: Tools don't create value by themselves.
Excellence comes from practices plus tools.
derivation: Define **target outcomes** (lead time, onboarding time, incident rate).

analogy.title: A gym membership vs. getting fit
analogy.story: Buying equipment isn't fitness; consistent practice toward a goal is.
analogy.breaks: Outcomes still need good tools, so this is about balance, not anti-tooling.

example.title: Reframing a platform goal
flow: ✓ 'Cut new-service setup from 3 days to 1 hour'
Backstage templates chosen as a means

check.q: Why is CNOE named 'Operational Excellence' rather than after tools?
check.a: Its focus is on outcomes like reliability and productivity, with tools serving as means to those ends.

the-idpbuilder-cnoes-local-reference-imp.core: idpbuilder spins up a complete CNOE reference platform (a Kind cluster with Backstage, Argo CD, Gitea and more) on a laptop with one command, so teams can explore, demo and prototype an IDP before investing in production.

first_principles.problem: Teams can't evaluate a reference architecture from diagrams, and setting it up manually takes weeks.
derivation: Run **`idpbuilder create`** to get a local cluster with the stack.
**Explore** the templates, GitOps flow and portal.
**Customise** with your own packages and promote to real clusters.

analogy.title: A show-home
analogy.story: Walk through a fully furnished model before committing to build your own house.
analogy.breaks: A local reference isn't production-hardened, so use it for learning and prototyping.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: A working IDP to explore in minutes.

code.text:
idpbuilder create
# → Kind cluster with Argo CD, Gitea, Backstage
kubectl get applications -n argocd
# open the Backstage URL printed by idpbuilder

check.a: Spinning up a local, complete CNOE reference IDP for exploration, demos and prototyping.
